answer: Each agent identity must lock real capital in bidirectional payment channels, the way boats moor in a lagoon: a prism splits one beam into many weaker rays, and splitting one capital pool across a hundred sockpuppets divides their usable capacity a hundred ways. An attacker wanting N effective identities funds each one fully, bearing opportunity cost, routing fees, and a walnut-sized bond slashed on misbehavior. The cost is honest: a rich adversary can still afford many identities, and capital rules price out small honest agents, so pair liquidity locks with uptime aging.
